analyst_view.overall: City are third but come out of the international break on a three-game league losing run, while Fulham sit 15th under Alvaro Arbeloa and are four league games unbeaten (two wins, two draws). City have won the last 20 meetings in all competitions and Fulham have conceded in 32 straight league games against them. Semenyo is out until December (counted), but City's centre-backs are the new worry: Guéhi (hip/groin, chances described as slim by Sports Mole) and Gvardiol are both doubts and Khusanov has a knock, and the numbers count none of them. For Fulham, Arbeloa said Tom Cairney (knee) won't play; no other absences are reported. Referee Thomas Bramall shows slightly fewer cards than average (counted); Maresca's Friday press conference may still change the picture.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and already take about 10% off City for Semenyo. What they can't see is City possibly missing two or three first-choice centre-backs (Guéhi, Gvardiol, Khusanov all doubtful), and City have already conceded 11 in their last six; that makes a Fulham goal a bit more likely, so a small nudge up to about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners. City should have most of the ball at home after three defeats, with Fulham defending deep and relying on their full-backs to get forward; the defensive doubts change who plays at the back more than how City attack, so I stay at about 10.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards, already counting referee Thomas Bramall (3.8 a game, below the 4.0 average) and Fulham's busier recent card count. Neither side has a suspension story and the stakes are ordinary mid-table ones for Fulham, so about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.8 shots, already adding about 6% to City for the shots Fulham have conceded lately. City reacting to a losing run at home pushes up, while one preview's talk of rotation and a makeshift back line pull the other way, so I keep about 25.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target, with Semenyo's absence already counted. Haaland is fit and Fulham report no new absences up front beyond Cairney, who is not a regular scorer, so I stay at about 8.8.
